messages.text: For a Wireless Communication use case involving Wi-Fi 7/8, where would Signal Generator / Signal Analyzer fit in the test workflow?

Signal Generator / Signal Analyzer fits mainly in the **non-signaling PHY/RF measurement part of the Wi‑Fi 7/8 workflow**, especially for waveform generation, RF Tx/Rx analysis, loopback validation, and production RF test—not as the main signaling/protocol tester role.[2][20]
| Workflow stage | Where SG / SA fits | Supported instruments / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| R&D signaling / device operation test | The primary tool is a signaling tester, not standalone SG/SA: R&S CMX500 is used for Wi‑Fi 7 R&D signaling, real-world RF TX/RX characteristics, MLO, multiple RF chains, 2x2 MIMO, coexistence, and E2E testing.[20] For Wi‑Fi 8, CMX500 is positioned for RF signaling tests and new hurdles such as dRU and UEQM.[10] | CMX500 one-box signaling tester for Wi‑Fi 7/8 signaling workflow.[10][20] |
| Non-signaling RF / PHY waveform test | SG/SA fits here as RF generator/analyzer capability: R&S CMP180 is a radio communication tester configurable with multi-port RF generator/analyzer, communication-standard measurement options, waveform options, and R&S VSE analysis capability.[2] | CMP180 RF generator/analyzer path.[2] |
| Production RF test | SG/SA fits strongly here: CMP180 is described as a production-phase non-signaling RF measurement tester supporting Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz, with bandwidths up to 500 MHz.[20] | CMP180 production non-signaling tester.[20] |
| Wi‑Fi 8 candidate / beyond-Wi‑Fi‑7 waveform validation | SG/SA-style waveform generation/analysis fits for loopback waveform validation: CMP180 will demonstrate verifying a 480 MHz WLAN waveform in loopback mode, described only as a potential waveform candidate for yet-to-be-defined Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn.[1][20] | CMP180 480 MHz loopback waveform validation; not proof of formal Wi‑Fi 8 bandwidth.[1][20] |
| MIMO / multi-RF-chain non-signaling scaling | CMP180 includes two analyzers, two generators, and two sets of eight RF ports in one box for 2x2 MIMO; two CMP180 units can be combined for four analyzers and generators for 4x4 MIMO access points.[20] | CMP180 multi-generator/analyzer MIMO production/R&D workflow.[20] |
| OTA Wi‑Fi 7 workflow | SG/SA is not the central element in the cited OTA Wi‑Fi 7 workflow; the cited OTA setup uses CMX500 signaling plus chamber/control software such as Bluetest Flow / Bluetest RTS or EMITE chambers for OTA measurements.[21][22] | CMX500 + OTA chamber workflow, not standalone SG/SA.[21][22] |
| Wi‑Fi over mmWave R&D variant | In the WoMT R&D setup, SG/SA appears in the Tx/Rx measurement path: the RD site uses R&S ATS1800C, R&S FSW67, and R&S SMM100A for Tx/Rx measurement.[7] However, the source has a noted model/spec inconsistency for SMM100A frequency range, so formal frequency capability must be checked against product specifications.[8] | FSW67 as analyzer and SMM100A as SG in WoMT R&D Tx/Rx measurement, with specification risk.[7][8] |
【推論】For a standard Wi‑Fi 7/8 wireless communication test flow, use CMX500 for signaling/protocol-style device operation tests, and place Signal Generator / Signal Analyzer capability around the CMP180-style non-signaling RF workflow for waveform generation, RF analysis, loopback, MIMO RF-chain validation, and production test.[2][10][20]
